object_entity.description: Jesus was truly conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary, not through natural human generation.

context_place.notes: Imperial capital associated with the Roman church and Paul later ministry.

evidence.notes: The eucharistic prayer references Christ born of the virgin.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The eucharistic prayer (anaphora): the bishop gives thanks over the bread and cup, reciting the narrative of institution; the people respond 'Amen'; the deacons present the offering. The prayer includes thanksgiving for creation, incarnation, passion, and resurrection.
passage.notes: Earliest surviving eucharistic prayer; structured anaphora with institution narrative and thanksgiving

source.title: Apostolic Tradition
source.author: Hippolytus of Rome (attributed)
source.notes: Church order with ordination rites, baptismal liturgy, and eucharistic prayer; Easton translation.

object_entity.proposition_label: Virginity and celibacy are honored as a positive Christian calling
object_entity.description: Virginity and celibacy are not merely tolerated but positively honored as a higher calling, even while marriage is defended as legitimate and good.

context_place.notes: Imperial capital associated with the Roman church and Paul later ministry.

evidence.notes: AT references virgins and widows as honored states.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Every faithful man and woman, when they have risen from sleep in the morning, before they touch any work, shall wash their hands and pray to God. If there is instruction in the word, let each one prefer to go there. Let them pray at the third hour, the sixth hour, the ninth hour, at bedtime, at midnight, and at cockcrow.
passage.notes: Fixed prayer hours throughout the day; daily prayer discipline for the faithful
